COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPSS No.675 of 2024
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Siddhartha Sah, learned counsel for the
petitioner.
2. Mr. C.K. Sharma, learned counsel for the respondent
no.1-Commission.
3. Mr. R.C. Joshi, learned Brief Holder for the
State/respondent no.2.
4. By means of this writ petition, petitioner has sought
indulgence of this Court for a direction to respondent no.1-
Commission to examine the video recording of driving test
of the petitioner held on 18.12.2023 and re-evaluate and
award correct marks to the petitioner as per norms and
criteria on the basis of the performance of the petitioner in
the driving test and include the petitioner in the provisional
merit list for document verification.
5. Facts of the case as disclosed from the writ petition
are that an advertisement dated 24.08.2021 was issued by
respondent no-1/Commission supplying the vacancies for
the post of Drivers in various departments of the State of
Uttarakhand. The petitioner submitted his candidature for
the post of driver pursuant to the aforesaid advertisement.
6. On 12.06.2022 written examination was held and the
petitioner claims to have found place in the Select
List/Merit List for driving test and he was ranked at Sr.
No.6.
7. The criteria for recruitment was that out of total 100
marks, there are 25 marks for written examination and 75
marks for driving test. It is an undisputed fact that the
petitioner scored 47.791 marks out of 100, while the last
man selected in the category to which the petitioner belongs
(General Category, Male Candidate) scored 60.458 marks
and therefore the petitioner did not find place in the final
Select List/Merit List. Feeling aggrieved the petitioner is
before this Court.
8. This Court vide order dated 22.04.2024 sought
instructions from the respondent-Commission, and on
instruction, the aforesaid situation has been clarified, that

2
the petitioner could not score more marks than the last man
selected in the category to which the petitioner belongs.
9. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the
petitioner has qualified in the driving test successfully and
he also answered all the questions correctly as asked by the
examiner and the entire test was video-graphed.
10. The petitioner casts doubt about having secured
28.611 marks out of 75 in the driving test.
11. Considering the rival contention of the parties, this
Court is not inclined to entertain the argument submitted by
learned counsel for the petitioner for the reason that the
Court is not an expert body, and in writ jurisdiction it
cannot be decided as to how the petitioner was driving
better than other candidates, who have been selected and
scored higher marks than the petitioner. Moreover the total
marks as stated above scored by the petitioner is far below
the marks obtained by the last man selected in the category,
to which the petitioner belongs (General Category Male
Candidate). Therefore the present writ petition lacks merit
and is thus dismissed.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 23.04.2024
